## What this is

**eShop ("AdventureWorks") — a .NET Aspire–orchestrated, services-based e‑commerce reference application** (`README.md:1-5`), targeting `net10.0` across the server projects (e.g. `src/Catalog.API/Catalog.API.csproj:3`).

## The single runnable entry point

There is **one entry point for the system**: the Aspire AppHost, `src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj` (`<Project Sdk="Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/13.2.0">`, `OutputType=Exe`, `src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj:1-3`). You run it with `dotnet run --project src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj`, or open `eShop.Web.slnf` in VS with AppHost as startup project (`README.md`, "Running the solution"). Its dashboard listens on `https://localhost:19888` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json:6`). The composition root is `builder = DistributedApplication.CreateBuilder(args) … builder.Build().Run()` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:3`, `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:101`).

## Processes started when the solution runs

Containers (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:7-13`): **redis**, **rabbitmq** ("eventbus", persistent lifetime), **postgres** (image `ankane/pgvector`, persistent) hosting four databases `catalogdb`, `identitydb`, `orderingdb`, `webhooksdb` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:15-18`).

.NET processes (each `AddProject<…>`):

| Aspire resource | Project | What composes it |
|---|---|---|
| `identity-api` | `src/Identity.API` (`Program.cs:21-23`) | ASP.NET MVC + Duende IdentityServer with in-memory clients/scopes, ASP.NET Identity on `identitydb`, auto-migration + `UsersSeed` (`src/Identity.API/Program.cs:1-41`) |
| `basket-api` | `src/Basket.API` (`Program.cs:28-31`) | gRPC-only service: `AddBasicServiceDefaults`, `MapGrpcService<BasketService>` (`src/Basket.API/Program.cs:1-14`); Redis-backed `RedisBasketRepository`, RabbitMQ subscription to `OrderStartedIntegrationEvent` (`src/Basket.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:12-21`) |
| `catalog-api` | `src/Catalog.API` (`Program.cs:33-35`) | Minimal API `MapCatalogApi`, versioned + OpenAPI (`src/Catalog.API/Program.cs:1-24`); pgvector `CatalogContext` + seed, integration-event log, RabbitMQ subscriptions, optional Ollama/OpenAI embedding generator (`src/Catalog.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:15-48`) |
| `ordering-api` | `src/Ordering.API` (`Program.cs:37-41`) | Versioned minimal API `MapOrdersApiV1` with auth (`src/Ordering.API/Program.cs:19-22`); MediatR + FluentValidation + logging/validator/transaction behaviors, EF `OrderingContext` with migrations/seed, 5 RabbitMQ subscriptions (`src/Ordering.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:16-59`) |
| `order-processor` | `src/OrderProcessor` (`Program.cs:43-46`) | Worker SDK (`src/OrderProcessor/OrderProcessor.csproj:1`); hosted `GracePeriodManagerService` + Npgsql data source + RabbitMQ (`src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:9-18`); waits for `ordering-api` because that owns the EF migrations (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:46`) |
| `payment-processor` | `src/PaymentProcessor` (`Program.cs:48-49`) | Event-only host: subscribes `OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEvent` (`src/PaymentProcessor/Program.cs:5-9`) |
| `webhooks-api` | `src/Webhooks.API` (`Program.cs:51-54`) | Versioned `MapWebHooksApiV1` (`src/Webhooks.API/Program.cs:19-21`); `WebhooksContext` on `webhooksdb`, sender/retriever/grant-url-tester, 3 RabbitMQ subscriptions (`src/Webhooks.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:5-23`) |
| `mobile-bff` | YARP reverse proxy resource (no project) | `builder.AddYarp("mobile-bff").ConfigureMobileBffRoutes(catalogApi, orderingApi, identityApi)` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:57-59`); route table in `src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:185-250` |
| `webhooksclient` | `src/WebhookClient` (`Program.cs:62-64`) | Blazor Server app + OIDC cookie auth against Identity, typed `WebhooksClient` HTTP client (`src/WebhookClient/Program.cs:1-31`, `src/WebhookClient/Extensions/Extensions.cs:12-22`) |
| `webapp` | `src/WebApp` (`Program.cs:66-74`) | The storefront: Blazor interactive-server Razor components (`src/WebApp/Program.cs:8`, `:30`), image forwarder to catalog (`src/WebApp/Program.cs:32`), gRPC `Basket.BasketClient`, HTTP clients to catalog/ordering, OIDC auth, 6 RabbitMQ order-status subscriptions (`src/WebApp/Extensions/Extensions.cs:15-50`) |

That is 9 project processes + 1 YARP proxy + 3 containers. Cross-cutting: every project calls `AddServiceDefaults()`/`AddBasicServiceDefaults()` from `src/eShop.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs:16-46` (OpenTelemetry, health checks, service discovery, resilient HTTP), and the AppHost injects `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` into every project (`src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:22-46`).

Optional, **off by default**: OpenAI/Azure OpenAI and Ollama resources are gated by `bool useOpenAI = false;` and `bool useOllama = false;` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:77-87`), so no AI container starts unless you flip those.

## Runnable things that the AppHost does *not* start

- `src/ClientApp` — .NET MAUI client (`TargetFrameworks` android/ios/maccatalyst/windows, `OutputType=Exe`, `src/ClientApp/ClientApp.csproj:3-6`), launched separately; it talks to the mobile BFF on port 11632 (`src/ClientApp/ViewModels/SettingsViewModel.cs:58`).
- `src/HybridApp` — MAUI Blazor Hybrid client (`src/HybridApp/HybridApp.csproj:1-6`), entry `MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp()` pointing at `http://localhost:11632/` (`src/HybridApp/MauiProgram.cs:9-13`). Neither appears in any `AddProject<…>` call in `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs`, nor in `eShop.Web.slnf`.
- Libraries only (no entry point): `EventBus`, `EventBusRabbitMQ`, `IntegrationEventLogEF`, `Ordering.Domain`, `Ordering.Infrastructure`, `WebAppComponents`, `eShop.ServiceDefaults` (all plain `Microsoft.NET.Sdk`/`Sdk.Razor`).
- Tests: `tests/Basket.UnitTests`, `tests/Ordering.UnitTests`, `tests/Catalog.FunctionalTests`, `tests/Ordering.FunctionalTests`, `tests/ClientApp.UnitTests` (`eShop.slnx:23-29`), plus Playwright end-to-end specs in `e2e/` driven by `playwright.config.ts`.

One caveat: `PaymentProcessor` uses `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` (`src/PaymentProcessor/PaymentProcessor.csproj:1`) but maps only default/health endpoints, so functionally it is a message-consumer process rather than an API.
